ashtavakra.1.11.m: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
roles: Points to the self that was never bound.
ashtavakra.1.11.sa: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥

ashtavakra.1.16.m: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
ashtavakra.1.16.sa: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥

ashtavakra.1.17.m: Be free of expectation, unchanging, self-reliant, cool at heart, deep in understanding and unshaken, resting in pure awareness alone.
ashtavakra.1.17.sa: निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः । अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥

ashtavakra.1.2.m: If you want freedom, my son, shun the objects of craving as you would poison, and take in forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth as you would nectar.
roles: Names daya, kindness, as one of the five.
ashtavakra.1.2.sa: मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज । क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥

ashtavakra.1.4.m: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
roles: Cultivates taking the self as awareness, distinct from the body.
ashtavakra.1.4.sa: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥

ashtavakra.1.5.m: You are not a brahmin or of any caste, not of any stage of life, not something the senses can grasp. Unattached and formless, the witness of everything, be happy.
ashtavakra.1.5.sa: न त्वं विप्रादिको वर्णो नाश्रमी नाक्षगोचरः । असङ्गोऽसि निराकारो विश्वसाक्षी सुखी भव ॥

ashtavakra.1.8.m: You have been bitten by the great black snake of the ego that says 'I am the doer'. Drink the nectar of trust that says 'I am not the doer', and be happy.
roles: Shows trust is the nectar offered.
ashtavakra.1.8.sa: अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः । नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥

ashtavakra.10.3.m: Wherever there is craving, know that the endless round is there. Take up mature dispassion, be free of craving, and be happy.
ashtavakra.10.3.sa: यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै । प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥

ashtavakra.10.7.m: Enough of wealth, of desire, even of good deeds. In this wilderness of life the mind never found rest in them.
roles: Shows the weariness is the ground of letting go.
ashtavakra.10.7.sa: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥

ashtavakra.10.8.m: Through how many births have you done hard, painful work with body, mind and speech? Now, at least, stop.
ashtavakra.10.8.sa: कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा । दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥

ashtavakra.11.1.m: One who knows for certain that becoming, being and ceasing happen by nature stays untroubled, free of pain, and easily finds peace.
ashtavakra.11.1.sa: भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी । निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥

ashtavakra.11.3.m: One who knows for certain that misfortune and good fortune come in their time by destiny is content, senses at rest, neither longing nor grieving.
ashtavakra.11.3.sa: आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी । तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥

ashtavakra.11.5.m: One who knows for certain that suffering here is born of worry and nothing else is free of it, happy, at peace, and unattached everywhere.
roles: Shows peace as one free of worry is at peace everywhere.
ashtavakra.11.5.sa: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥

ashtavakra.13.1.m: The ease of owning nothing is rare even for one who wears only a loincloth. So I have let go of both renouncing and acquiring, and live happily.
ashtavakra.13.1.sa: अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् । त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥

ashtavakra.13.3.m: Seeing truly that nothing done is ever really done by me, I do whatever comes to be done and live happily.
ashtavakra.13.3.sa: कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥

ashtavakra.15.1.m: A clear-minded person is fulfilled by even a simple teaching; another stays confused despite a lifetime of inquiry.
roles: Shows a clear mind taking the teaching at once.
ashtavakra.15.1.sa: यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् । आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥

ashtavakra.15.10.m: Let the body last till the end of the age, or let it go today: what gain or loss is that to you, who are pure awareness?
roles: Shows no gain or loss to the self.
ashtavakra.15.10.sa: देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः । क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥

ashtavakra.15.11.m: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
roles: Shows the self as the ocean in which the world rises.
ashtavakra.15.11.sa: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥

ashtavakra.15.19.m: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
roles: Shows the self is called ananda-vigraha.
ashtavakra.15.19.sa: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥

ashtavakra.15.2.m: Liberation is losing your taste for the objects of craving; bondage is relishing them. That is all there is to know; now do as you wish.
roles: Shows liberation as the taste going.
ashtavakra.15.2.sa: मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः । एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥

ashtavakra.15.4.m: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness itself, the ever-present witness, needing nothing. Live happily.
roles: Names awareness, the witness, is what you are.
ashtavakra.15.4.sa: न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् । चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥

ashtavakra.15.5.m: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind. You are awareness itself, free of thought-forms and unchanging. Live happily.
roles: Gives the self as awareness free of thought-forms.
ashtavakra.15.5.sa: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥

ashtavakra.15.8.m: Have faith, my son, have faith. Do not be confused about this. You are knowledge itself, the Lord, the Self beyond nature.
roles: Shows jnana-svarupa, the self beyond prakriti.
ashtavakra.15.8.sa: श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः । ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥

ashtavakra.15.9.m: The body, made of nature's qualities, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither comes nor goes. Why grieve for it?
roles: Shows the self is beyond coming and going.
ashtavakra.15.9.sa: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥

ashtavakra.16.1.m: My son, you may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, but you will not be at ease until you forget them all.
roles: Svasthya, ease, comes from letting go of it all.
ashtavakra.16.1.sa: आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः । तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥

ashtavakra.16.10.m: One who is proud even of being liberated, and possessive about the body, is neither wise nor a yogi, only a sufferer.
roles: Shows no mine-ness even toward the body.
ashtavakra.16.10.sa: यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा । न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥

ashtavakra.16.2.m: Wise one, enjoy, work or meditate as you will: your mind will still long for that state where every want has dropped away.
roles: Shows the deepest wish is the end of wanting.
ashtavakra.16.2.sa: भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते । चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥

ashtavakra.16.3.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
roles: Nirvriti, peace, follows on seeing it.
ashtavakra.16.3.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

ashtavakra.16.9.m: The attached person wants to escape the world to get away from pain. The one free of attachment has no pain and is not troubled even while in it.
roles: Shows freedom from raga making place irrelevant.
ashtavakra.16.9.sa: हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया । वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥

ashtavakra.17.1.m: The one who is content, senses clear, always happy alone, has gained the fruit of knowledge and of yoga practice.
roles: Names delighting in his own company.
ashtavakra.17.1.sa: तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा । तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥

ashtavakra.17.4.m: One who doesn't keep dwelling on pleasures already enjoyed, nor pine for pleasures not yet had, is rare in this world.
roles: Shows the rare one content with what is.
ashtavakra.17.4.sa: यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः । अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥

ashtavakra.17.7.m: He neither longs for the world to end nor resents its going on; so the blessed one lives happily on whatever livelihood comes.
ashtavakra.17.7.sa: वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ । यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥

ashtavakra.18.100.m: The calm mind does not run off to crowded places or to the forest. Whatever and wherever, it stays the same.
ashtavakra.18.100.sa: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥

ashtavakra.18.11.m: For the yogi of steady nature there is no difference between ruling a kingdom and living on alms, gain and loss, the crowd and the forest.
ashtavakra.18.11.sa: स्वाराज्ये भैक्षवृत्तौ च लाभालाभे जने वने । निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य न विशेषोऽस्ति योगिनः ॥

ashtavakra.18.2.m: One may earn every kind of wealth and enjoy abundant pleasures, but without letting go of everything, no one is happy.
ashtavakra.18.2.sa: अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् । न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥

ashtavakra.18.20.m: The steady person has no stubborn attachment to doing or to not doing. Doing whatever comes to be done, he stays at ease.
ashtavakra.18.20.sa: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥

ashtavakra.18.3.m: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
roles: Shows calm as rain that cools.

ashtavakra.18.39.m: The confused person never finds peace, because he is trying to get it. The wise, clear about the truth, is always calm.
roles: Shows calm following clear knowing, not effort.
ashtavakra.18.39.sa: न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति । धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥

ashtavakra.18.55.m: Mocked and scolded by servants, children, spouses, grandchildren and relatives, the yogi is not the least disturbed.
ashtavakra.18.55.sa: भृत्यैः पुत्रैः कलत्रैश्च दौहित्रैश्चापि गोत्रजैः । विहस्य धिक्कृतो योगी न याति विकृतिं मनाक् ॥

ashtavakra.18.58.m: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
ashtavakra.18.58.sa: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥

ashtavakra.18.59.m: He sits happily, sleeps happily, comes and goes happily, speaks and eats happily: calm-minded even in daily affairs.
ashtavakra.18.59.sa: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥

ashtavakra.18.61.m: Even a fool's retreat from action turns into activity; even a wise person's activity bears the fruit of stillness.
ashtavakra.18.61.sa: निवृत्तिरपि मूढस्य प्रवृत्ति रुपजायते । प्रवृत्तिरपि धीरस्य निवृत्तिफलभागिनी ॥

ashtavakra.18.81.m: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
roles: Shows same in gain and loss.
ashtavakra.18.81.sa: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥

ashtavakra.18.91.m: Beggar or king, whoever is free of desire shines, the one for whom things have stopped looking 'good' or 'bad'.
roles: Good and bad notions have fallen away.
ashtavakra.18.91.sa: भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते । भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥

ashtavakra.18.98.m: The free one is at ease in whatever state he finds himself, done with what needed doing; even everywhere, free of craving, he does not dwell on what he did or left undone.
ashtavakra.18.98.sa: मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः । समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥

ashtavakra.18.99.m: Praised, he is not pleased; blamed, he is not angry. He neither dreads death nor clings to life.
ashtavakra.18.99.sa: न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति । नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥

ashtavakra.2.14.m: How wonderful I am! I bow to myself: I own nothing at all, or else everything that speech and mind can reach is mine.
ashtavakra.2.14.sa: अहो अहं नमो मह्यं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन । अथवा यस्य मे सर्वं यद् वाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥

ashtavakra.3.1.m: Knowing yourself truly as one and indestructible, wise and steady as you are, how can you still delight in piling up wealth?
roles: Shows the indestructible self needs nothing.
ashtavakra.3.1.sa: अविनाशिनमात्मानमेकं विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः । तवात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य कथमर्थार्जने रतिः ॥

scene.s: Ashtavakra probes whether Janaka's insight is real: if you know you are whole, why still chase wealth, run like a beggar, or care about praise and blame? He sketches the steady person who is neither elated nor angered.

ashtavakra.3.10.m: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's: how could praise or blame disturb such a large-hearted person?
roles: Shows being unshaken by praise and blame.
ashtavakra.3.10.sa: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥

ashtavakra.3.11.m: Seeing this world as a mere show and losing all fascination with it, how could a steady mind be afraid, even with death close by?
roles: Shows no fear even at death.
ashtavakra.3.11.sa: मायामात्रमिदं विश्वं पश्यन् विगतकौतुकः । अपि सन्निहिते मृत्यौ कथं त्रस्यति धीरधीः ॥

scene.s: Ashtavakra probes whether Janaka's insight is real: if you know you are whole, why still chase wealth, run like a beggar, or care about praise and blame? He sketches the steady person who is neither elated nor angered.

ashtavakra.3.12.m: Who can compare with the great soul whose mind wants nothing even when hopes collapse, content in knowing the Self?
ashtavakra.3.12.sa: निःस्पृहं मानसं यस्य नैराश्येऽपि महात्मनः । तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥

ashtavakra.3.14.m: For one who has dropped inner stains, free of opposites and of wishes, whatever pleasure comes by chance brings neither pain nor elation.
roles: Shows nirdvandva, neither pain nor elation.
ashtavakra.3.14.sa: अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः । यदृच्छयागतो भोगो न दुःखाय न तुष्टये ॥

ashtavakra.3.3.m: Knowing 'I am That in which this world rises like waves on the sea', why do you run around like a beggar?
roles: Shows I am That in which the world rises.
ashtavakra.3.3.sa: विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे । सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥

scene.s: Ashtavakra probes whether Janaka's insight is real: if you know you are whole, why still chase wealth, run like a beggar, or care about praise and blame? He sketches the steady person who is neither elated nor angered.

ashtavakra.5.4.m: Be the same in pain and pleasure, complete, equal in hope and despair, equal in life and death; like this, dissolve now.
roles: Gives sama in every pair including life and death.
ashtavakra.5.4.sa: समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः । समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥

ashtavakra.8.1.m: It is bondage when the mind wants something, grieves over something, drops or grabs something, is pleased or angered by something. It is freedom when the mind does not want, grieve, drop, grab, delight or rage.
roles: Shows a mind that neither takes up nor throws off.
ashtavakra.8.1.sa: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥

ashtavakra.8.4.m: When there is no 'I', there is freedom; when there is 'I', there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, grab nothing and push nothing away.
ashtavakra.8.4.sa: यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा । मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥

ashtavakra.9.1.m: For whom, and when, have the pairs of 'done' and 'not yet done' ever come to rest? Knowing this, through disenchantment become free, indifferent even to vows and rules.
ashtavakra.9.1.sa: कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा । एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥

ashtavakra.9.4.m: What time or age of life is free of ups and downs? Let them be, take what comes, and you reach fulfilment.
roles: Shows upeksha, letting the pairs be.
ashtavakra.9.4.sa: कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् । तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥

ashtavakra.9.5.m: Seeing how differently the great sages, saints and yogis think, who would not grow weary of the argument and become calm?
ashtavakra.9.5.sa: नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा । दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥

avadhuta.1.18.m: Ah, mind, why do you run around confused like a ghost? See the Self as undivided, drop attachment, and be happy.
avadhuta.1.18.sa: अहो चित्त कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् । अभिन्नं पश्य चात्मानं रागत्यागात्सुखी भव ॥

avadhuta.1.68.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
avadhuta.1.68.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥

avadhuta.2.1.m: Whether the teacher is young, given to pleasures, unlearned, a servant or a householder, do not dwell on it. Who throws away a jewel because it fell in dirt?
roles: Takes the jewel, not the wrapping.
avadhuta.2.1.sa: बालस्य वा विषयभोगरतस्य वापि मूर्खस्य सेवकजनस्य गृहस्थितस्य । एतद्गुरोः किमपि नैव न चिन्तनीयं रत्नं कथं त्यजति कोऽप्यशुचौ प्रविष्टम् ॥

avadhuta.2.2.m: Do not look here for poetic merit; the wise take only the essence. A boat without vermilion paint or decoration still carries across those who want to cross.
avadhuta.2.2.sa: नैवात्र काव्यगुण एव तु चिन्तनीयो ग्राह्यः परं गुणवता खलु सार एव । सिन्दूरचित्ररहिता भुवि रूपशून्या पारं न किं नयति नौरिह गन्तुकामान् ॥

avadhuta.2.24.m: One free of attachment and aversion, devoted to the good of all beings, firm in understanding and steady, reaches the highest state.
avadhuta.2.24.sa: रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः । दृढबोधश्च धीरश्च स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् ॥

avadhuta.2.7.m: Thoughts arise and dissolve on their own, like bubbles in water; what is there for me to do about them?
avadhuta.2.7.sa: प्रमादेन न सन्देहः किं करिष्यामि वृत्तिमान् । उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते बुद्बुदाश्च यथा जले ॥

avadhuta.3.34.m: Why do you weep, friend? You have no old age, no death. Why weep, friend? Birth is no sorrow to you. Why weep, friend? You do not change.
roles: Shows the self as unchanging and sky-like.
avadhuta.3.34.sa: किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न जरा न मृत्युः किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च जन्म दुःखम् । किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विकारो ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥

avadhuta.3.46.m: Let go, let go of the world, and let go of renouncing it too. Renouncing and not renouncing are both poison; your nature is pure, natural nectar.
avadhuta.3.46.sa: मुञ्च मुञ्च हि संसारं त्यागं मुञ्च हि सर्वथा । त्यागात्यागविषं शुद्धममृतं सहजं ध्रुवम् ॥

avadhuta.7.9.m: Free of union and separation, the yogi; free of enjoying and refusing, the enjoyer: so he walks slowly, slowly, in the natural joy of the mind.
avadhuta.7.9.sa: योगवियोगै रहितो योगी भोगविभोगै रहितो भोगी । एवं चरति हि मन्दं मन्दं मनसा कल्पितसहजानन्दम् ॥

avadhuta.8.2.m: The sage is unshaken by desires, self-restrained, gentle, pure, owns nothing, seeks nothing, eats moderately, is calm, steady, and has taken refuge in Me.
avadhuta.8.2.sa: कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो मृदुः शुचिरकिञ्चनः । अनीहो मितभुक् शान्तः स्थिरो मच्छरणो मुनिः ॥

avadhuta.8.3.m: Alert, deep, steadfast, master of the six waves of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; seeking no honour yet honouring others; capable, friendly, compassionate, wise.
avadhuta.8.3.sa: अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः । अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥

avadhuta.8.4.m: Compassionate, harming no one, patient with all beings, true to the core, blameless, even-minded, helpful to all.

avadhuta.8.6.m: Free of the noose of expectation, pure at beginning, middle and end, always living in joy: that is the meaning of the syllable 'A'.
avadhuta.8.6.sa: आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः । आनन्दे वर्तते नित्यमकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥

avadhuta.8.7.m: One who has given up old cravings, whose speech is wholesome, and who lives in the present: that is the meaning of 'va'.
roles: Shows dwelling in what is present.
avadhuta.8.7.sa: वासना वर्जिता येन वक्तव्यं च निरामयम् । वर्तमानेषु वर्तेत वकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥

dheesh_gita.1.4.m: The Father of the world, its friend, the Lord who protects all, standing beyond the intellect, out of compassion presides over the intellect; loving those who come to him for refuge, he gives beings freedom. So all the Vedas call him Dheesh.
roles: He loves those who come for refuge.
dheesh_gita.1.4.sa: जगत्पिता जगद्वन्धुर्भगवान विश्वपालकः । परे बुद्धे: स्थितो बुद्धिमधिष्ठाय कृपावशात् ॥ मुक्तिं ददाति जीवेभ्यः शरणागतवत्सलः । अतः सम्प्रोच्यते धीश आम्नायैरखिलैरसौ ॥

dheesh_gita.1.42.m: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.
dheesh_gita.1.42.sa: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥

dheesh_gita.1.46.m: Though I am all-pervading, devotees full of feeling see me in many forms, as they wish, and are fulfilled. I am without form, sages, yet my faithful devotees see me in a bodily form, or as light.
roles: Shows devotion fulfils itself in whatever form it sees.
dheesh_gita.1.46.sa: विभुं मामप्यहो भक्ता भावुकाः स्वेच्छया द्विजाः। नानारूपेषु पश्यन्ति कृतकृत्या भवन्ति च ॥ रूपहीनोऽस्म्यहं विप्राः ! श्रद्धावन्तस्तथापि मे । भक्ता मां स्थूलरूपे वा ज्योतीरूपे निरीक्ष्य च ॥

dheesh_gita.4.19.m: Truly, wise ones, by the dharma-filled motherly nature of my Prakriti, beings are protected and nourished without end.
dheesh_gita.4.19.sa: निश्चितं मातृभावेन विज्ञाः ! धर्ममयेण मे। प्रकृतेः पालिता जीवाः पोपिताश्च निरन्तरम् ॥

dheesh_gita.7.27.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
dheesh_gita.7.27.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

hans_gita.10.m: If another pierces him hard with arrows of harsh words, he should stay calm. The one who stays cheerful though provoked takes the provoker's merit for himself.
hans_gita.10.r: Hamsa Gita 10 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.10 in our data)
roles: Shows staying calm under verbal attack.
hans_gita.10.sa: परश्चेदेनमति वादबानैर्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः । संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिहृष्यते यः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥

hans_gita.11.m: One who holds back the blazing anger stirred by an insult or a wounding slight, who stays clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.
hans_gita.11.r: Hamsa Gita 11 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.11 in our data)
hans_gita.11.sa: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥

hans_gita.17.m: One who, though spoken to harshly, answers neither harshly nor with flattery, who when struck does not strike back out of steadiness, and wishes no harm to the one who hurt him: the gods long for such a person.
hans_gita.17.r: Hamsa Gita 17 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.17 in our data)
roles: Dhairya is named as the reason.
hans_gita.17.sa: यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् । पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तुस्तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्ते सदैव ॥

hans_gita.21.m: Freed from wrongs like the moon from dark clouds, spotless and steady, waiting for the right time, the wise one succeeds through patience.
hans_gita.21.r: Hamsa Gita 21 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.21 in our data)
roles: Dhairya is named as the means.
hans_gita.21.sa: विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो धनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥

hans_gita.25.m: A wise person should not answer the ignorant with abuse and insult. So do not inflame the other, and do not harm yourself.
hans_gita.25.r: Hamsa Gita 25 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.25 in our data)
hans_gita.25.sa: आक्रोशनावमानाभ्यां नाबुधान् गर्हयेद् बुधः । तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥

hans_gita.26.m: The wise should feel as satisfied by an insult as by nectar. The one insulted sleeps in peace; the one who insults is ruined.
hans_gita.26.r: Hamsa Gita 26 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.26 in our data)
hans_gita.26.sa: अमृतस्येव सन्तृप्येदवमानस्य वै द्विजः । सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥

hans_gita.31.m: Going among humans and gods, I tell them all: truth is the ladder to heaven, as a boat is the way across the sea.
hans_gita.31.r: Hamsa Gita 31 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.31 in our data)
roles: Gives a clear assurance about where truth leads.
hans_gita.31.sa: आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसञ्चरन् । सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥

hans_gita.40.m: The world is covered by ignorance; it does not shine because of envy; people abandon friends out of greed, and miss heaven through attachment.
hans_gita.40.r: Hamsa Gita 40 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.40 in our data)
hans_gita.40.sa: अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥

hans_gita.42.m: The wise one alone is happy among people; the wise one alone can stay quiet among many; the wise one alone is strong though weak; the wise one alone stays out of their quarrels.
hans_gita.42.r: Hamsa Gita 42 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.42 in our data)
hans_gita.42.sa: प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां प्राज्ञश्चैको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । प्राज्ञ एको बलवान् दुर्बलोऽपि प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥

hans_gita.7.m: This is the work, you who seek immortality: austerity, self-control, truth and guarding yourself. Untie all the knots of the heart and bring likes and dislikes under your own control.
hans_gita.7.r: Hamsa Gita 7 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.7 in our data)
hans_gita.7.sa: इदं कार्यममृताशाः श‍ृणोमि तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः । ग्रन्थीन् विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वान् प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥

ram_gita.24.m: With faith, through the words 'You are That' and the grace of the teacher, a pure-minded person who knows the oneness of the Self and the individual becomes happy and unshakable like Mount Meru.
roles: Shows oneness of atman and jiva.
ram_gita.24.sa: श्रद्धान्वितस्तत्त्वमसीति वाक्यतो गुरोः प्रसादादपि शुद्धमानसः । विज्ञाय चैकात्म्यमथात्मजीवयोः सुखी भवेन्मेरुरिवाप्रकम्पनः ॥

ram_gita.34.m: Having set everything aside with 'not this, not this' and tasted the nectar of awareness in the heart, let the whole world go once its essence is taken, as one drinks the water and then puts down the coconut.
roles: Shows chidghana, dense awareness, tasted in the heart.
ram_gita.34.sa: नेतिप्रमाणेन निराकृताखिलो हृदा समास्वादितचिद्घनामृतः । त्यजेदशेषं जगदात्तसद्रसं पीत्वा यथाम्भः प्रजहाति तत्फलम् ॥

ram_gita.35.m: The Self is never born and never dies; it does not wane or grow. Ancient, beyond all comparison, blissful, self-luminous, all-pervading, one without a second.
roles: Gives a full description of the self.
ram_gita.35.sa: कदाचिदात्मा न मृतो न जायते न क्षीयते नापि विवर्धतेऽनवः । निरस्तसर्वातिशयः सुखात्मकः स्वयम्प्रभः सर्वगतोऽयमद्वयः ॥

ram_gita.37.m: The wise call it superimposition when, through confusion, one thing is taken for another, as a snake is seen in a rope; so the world is seen in the Lord.
roles: Shows the rope is seen as rope.
ram_gita.37.sa: यदन्यदन्यत्र विभाव्यते भ्रमादध्यासमित्याहुरमुं विपश्चितः । असर्पभूतेऽहिविभावनं यथा रज्ज्वादिके तद्वदपीश्वरे जगत् ॥

ram_gita.39.m: Desire, attachment, pleasure and the rest belong to the mind and keep us bound. In deep sleep they are absent, and then the Self is felt simply as happiness.
roles: Names the self known as sukha-svarupa from deep sleep.
ram_gita.39.sa: इच्छादिरागादि सुखादिधर्मिकाः सदा धियः संसृतिहेतवः परे । यस्मात्प्रसुप्तौ तदभावतः परः सुखस्वरूपेण विभाव्यते हि नः ॥

ram_gita.46.m: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
roles: Names the self as the object of contemplation.
ram_gita.46.sa: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥

ram_gita.5.m: I take refuge at your lotus feet, Lord, which free one from the world and which yogis meditate on. Teach me so that I may easily and happily cross this endless ocean of ignorance.
ram_gita.5.sa: अहं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि पदाम्बुजं प्रभो भवापवर्गं तव योगिभावितम् । यथाञ्जसाज्ञानमपारवारिधिं सुखं तरिष्यामि तथानुशाधि माम् ॥

ram_gita.52.m: Always absorbed in the sense of the supreme Self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, he lives radiating that inner happiness, free, like an ocean of still water.
ram_gita.52.sa: एवं सदा जातपरात्मभावनः स्वानन्दतुष्टः परिविस्मृताखिलः । आस्ते स नित्यात्मसुखप्रकाशकः साक्षाद्विमुक्तोऽचलवारिसिन्धुवत् ॥

ram_gita.58.m: Until one sees everything as Me, one should be devoted to worshipping Me. To the person of faith and strong devotion, I am visible in the heart day and night.
ram_gita.58.sa: यावन्न पश्येदखिलं मदात्मकं तावन्मदाराधनतत्परो भवेत् । श्रद्धालुरत्यूर्जितभक्तिलक्षणो यस्तस्य दृश्योऽहमहर्निशं हृदि ॥

ram_gita.61.m: Whoever serves me in the heart, now and then, whether as beyond qualities or with qualities, becomes me; with the dust of his feet he purifies the three worlds, as the sun does.
ram_gita.61.sa: यः सेवते मामगुणं गुणात्परं हृदा कदा वा यदि वा गुणात्मकम् । सोऽहं स्वपादाञ्चितरेणुभिः स्पृशन् पुनाति लोकत्रितयं यथा रविः ॥

shakti_gita.1.39.m: Carried away by the rush of feeling, we have tried to put into words what lies beyond word, mind and thought; forgive us this fault, treasure of kindness. Even in this forgiving, the cause is only your great, boundless grace, Mother. Mother of the world, whose form is Brahman, we bow to you, the compassionate, always.
roles: Names forgiveness itself as recognized grace.
shakti_gita.1.39.sa: परं मनोवेगविमोदिता वयं भावं भवत्या अपि वांगमनोधियाम । अगोचरं द्योतयितुं समुद्यताः क्षमस्व नो दोषममुं दयानिधे ! ॥ अत्र क्षमाप्तावपि कारणं ते महत्यपारास्ति कृपैव मातः! । ब्रह्मस्वरूपे ! जगदम्बिकेऽलं दयामयीं तवां सततं नमामः ॥

shakti_gita.1.47.m: Mother, there is no limit to your true grace. Your devotees who cannot see your form of feeling, for lack of complete understanding, you wish to favour with your natural glances of grace; you show yourself to them and give them both freedom and well-being.
shakti_gita.1.47.sa: नास्यम्ब ! सीमा तव सत्कृपायाः शक्ता न ये भक्तगणास्त्वदीयाः। तत्त्वप्रबोधस्य प्रपूर्त्यभावाद्रष्टुं हि ते भावमयस्वरूपम् ॥ स्वाभाविकैरेव कृपाकटाक्षैः समीहमाना ह्यनुकम्पितुं तान्। गुणाश्रयायच्छसि दर्शनं स्वं मुक्तिञ्च तेभ्योऽभ्युदयं ददासि ॥

shakti_gita.1.51.m: Those who, with undivided devotion alone, hover like bees at your lotus feet, Mother, you never let slip from the sight of you, that mine of freedom.
shakti_gita.1.51.sa: अनन्यभक्सैव तु केवलं हि भृङ्गायमाणास्तव पादपद्यमे। विच्योतयस्यम्ब ! न तानपि त्वं स्वदर्शनान्मोक्षखनेः कदापि ॥

shakti_gita.5.133.m: Gods, take up that pure dependence on me; take my shelter. As my devotees, always do your work joined to me.
shakti_gita.5.133.sa: मत्परायणतां पुण्यां गृणीताश्रयणं मम । मद्भक्ताः सततं कर्म मयुक्ताः कुरुतामराः ! ॥

shakti_gita.5.137.m: Sheltered by that, my devotees go beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, engaged in fitting work; they become free of wrong, devoted to me.
shakti_gita.5.137.sa: तदाश्रयेण मद्भक्ता द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः । युक्तकर्मरताः सन्तो निषपापा मत्परायणाः ॥

shakti_gita.6.149.m: For my wise devotees, gods, Nature in the form of knowledge frees them from all their actions, makes them her own, holds the devotee in her lap, and, to bring about his good, merges into me.
roles: Names vidya-svarupini, knowledge itself carries them.
shakti_gita.6.149.sa: ज्ञानिनां मम भक्तानां देवाः ! विद्यास्वरूपिणी। विमुच्य प्रकृतिस्तेभ्यः कर्माणि निखिलानि वै ॥ स्वायत्तानि प्रकुर्वन्ती भक्तानचं विभ्रती। तत्कल्याणकदम्बञ्च विधातुं लीयते मयि ॥

shakti_gita.6.27.m: But when those beings come to my refuge, I draw them toward me in many different ways.
roles: Acts on the one who turns.
shakti_gita.6.27.sa: परन्तु तेषु जीवेषु शरणं मे गतेषु वै । अहं नानाप्रकारेस्तानाकर्षामि स्वसम्मुखे ॥

shakti_gita.7.118.m: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the mother, the dwelling, the refuge, the friend; the origin, the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house, the imperishable seed.
shakti_gita.7.118.sa: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुर्माता निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवालयस्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥

shambhu_gita.2.43.m: My gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world. She is eternal and always works for the good of the universe.
roles: Names trust in a protecting order.
shambhu_gita.2.43.sa: विश्वं रक्षति मच्छक्तिः सात्त्विकी धर्मरूपिणी। नित्या सा वर्तते नित्यं विश्वकल्याणकारिणी ॥

shambhu_gita.6.75.m: Devotees who know the Self surely cross the ocean of sorrow. The one God is hidden in all beings; there is no doubt.
shambhu_gita.6.75.sa: तरन्त्यात्मविदो भक्ता निश्चितं शोकसागरम् । सर्वभूतेषु गूढोऽस्ति देव एको न संशयः ॥

shambhu_gita.6.91.m: When my distressed, my seeking and my wanting devotees take refuge in me, my nature takes on the feeling of a mother. Giving them the fulfilment they long for, she moves them forward toward me in every way. Do not wonder at this.
shambhu_gita.6.91.sa: यदाऽऽर्ताऽर्थाणिजिज्ञासुभक्ता मच्छरणागताः। स्युस्तदा प्रकृतिर्मेऽसौ मातृभावं समाश्रिता ॥ तेभ्यो वै बाञ्छिताः सिद्धीर्दत्त्वाऽग्रे सारयेदिमान्। सर्वतः सर्वथा कल्याः ! नैव कार्योऽत्र विस्मयः ॥

shambhu_gita.7.53.m: Dweller in the shrine of devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge. Do now, divine Shambhu, whatever will quickly bring us good here.
shambhu_gita.7.53.sa: विहारिन् ! विभो ! भक्तचेतोनिकेते शरण्यं किलैकान्ततस्त्वां व्रजामः । यथा नो भवेदत्र कल्याणमाशु तदेवाधुना देव ! शम्भो ! विधेहि ॥

shambhu_gita.7.65.m: I tell you an easy way; listen. Holding to this best of means, even while engaged in the hardest of tasks, you will not turn away from devotion to me.
roles: Shows devotion never turning from bhakti.
shambhu_gita.7.65.sa: उच्यते सुगमोपायः श्रूयतां विश्वभूतिदाः। वरिष्ठं यं समालम्ब्य कृच्छ्राव कृच्छ्रतरेप्वपि ॥ सक्ताः कार्येषु मद्भक्तेर्विमुखा न भविष्यथ । नूनमेकोऽद्वितीयोऽपि स्वभक्तेभ्यो निरन्तरम् ॥

scene.s: Bewildered by Shiva's limitless form, the ancestors praise him and finally hand him the outcome: do whatever is truly good for us. Shiva tells them their work needs a mind joined to him, then gives an easy way: see him everywhere, even in a loving embrace, so devotion never lapses amid hard work.
scene.t: The ancestors' hymn to Shiva and his easy way

shambhu_gita.7.80.m: Among the touches worthy of reverence, O best of ancestors, I am the embrace filled with love, affection, devotion and faith.
shambhu_gita.7.80.sa: प्रेम्णा स्नेहेन भक्तया च श्रद्धयाऽपि प्रपूरितम् । स्पर्शेषु तु नमस्येष्वालिङ्गनं पितृपुङ्गवाः ! ॥

st.bhakti.tulsi_abandoned_as_a_child.l: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
st.bhakti.tulsi_abandoned_as_a_child.s: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
st.bhakti.tulsi_abandoned_as_a_child.t: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

st.gitas.ashtavakra_tests_janaka.l: Real understanding shows in behaviour: less chasing, less rattled by praise and blame.
st.gitas.ashtavakra_tests_janaka.s: Ashtavakra probes whether Janaka's insight is real: if you know you are whole, why still chase wealth, run like a beggar, or care about praise and blame? He sketches the steady person who is neither elated nor angered.

st.gitas.avadhuta_why_do_you_weep.l: In grief, remember there is something in you that loss cannot touch.
st.gitas.avadhuta_why_do_you_weep.s: In a long hymn with the refrain 'I am the nectar of knowledge, vast as the sky', Dattatreya asks a friend again and again why he weeps, since what he truly is does not age, die or change.

st.gitas.gods_grow_comfortable.l: Every gain brings its own fear; holding things lightly is the way out.
st.gitas.gods_grow_comfortable.s: The frightened gods ask Vishnu how to become fearless. He explains that every possession carries its own fear (the body fears age, wealth fears thieves, power fears critics) and that only dispassion is free of fear; then he restates Bhagavad Gita 2.14-15 on enduring pleasure and pain.
st.gitas.gods_grow_comfortable.t: Vishnu on where fear comes from

st.gitas.janaka_asks_ashtavakra.l: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
st.gitas.janaka_asks_ashtavakra.s: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
st.gitas.janaka_asks_ashtavakra.t: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free

st.gitas.janaka_how_long_i_was_fooled.l: Seeing clearly can feel like waking up: nothing changed outside, everything changed inside.
st.gitas.janaka_how_long_i_was_fooled.s: Hearing the first teaching, Janaka bursts into wonder: he sees he has been fooled by confusion for years. He describes owning nothing and everything, and losing his fear.

st.gitas.janaka_tired_of_doing.l: Happiness can be simple: do what comes, stop both grabbing and renouncing.
st.gitas.janaka_tired_of_doing.s: In three short chapters Janaka describes how he has become calm: tired of busy body, speech and thought, he no longer renounces or grabs, and simply does what comes and lives happily.

st.gitas.lakshmana_private_question.l: Even the closest companion needs to ask; with faith and guidance, you can become steady.
st.gitas.lakshmana_private_question.s: After the war and his coronation, Rama is sitting alone when Lakshmana bows and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama teaches him that knowledge, not ritual alone, frees a person, and that faith and a teacher make one steady as a mountain.

st.gitas.learned_seers_no_peace.l: Learning alone may not settle the heart; turning to God can.
st.gitas.learned_seers_no_peace.s: Seers who had received all the Vedas still found no peace, so they went to Ganesha's world and took refuge in him. Ganesha tells them that though he has no form, loving devotees see him in the form they long for, and that knowing his highest form brings lasting peace.
st.gitas.learned_seers_no_peace.t: Learned seers find no peace and go to Ganesha

st.gitas.swan_on_insults.l: When insulted, staying calm protects you more than hitting back.
st.gitas.swan_on_insults.s: The swan teaches that words are arrows, that answering insult with insult only inflames both sides, and that the person who stays calm and wishes no harm sleeps in peace while the insulter carries the damage.

surya_gita.3.36.m: When a person has tasted pleasure and pain until he is weary of them, he becomes discerning and reaches freedom from craving.
surya_gita.3.36.sa: सुखदुःखोपभोगेन यदा निर्वेदमागतः। निष्कामत्वमवाप्नोति स्वविवेक पुरस्सरम् ॥

surya_gita.7.54.m: Great suffering comes to the one who has a busy mind; how could it touch one beyond the mind? It is the mind that makes the resolves that bring pain.
roles: Shows beyond the mind, no suffering.
surya_gita.7.54.sa: समनस्कान् महद्दु:खममनस्कस्यं तत्कुत:। समनस्को हि संकल्पान कुरुते दुखकारिणः ॥

vishnu_gita.1.58.m: By your being alone, O God, we exist and are yours; though we depend on you, we fools forget you through maya.
roles: Shows we exist by your being.
vishnu_gita.1.58.sa: तवैव सत्तया देव ! सत्तावन्तो वयं तव । आश्रिता आपि मूढास्त्वां विस्मरामो हि मायया ॥

vishnu_gita.1.60.m: We have come to you for refuge, you who love those who come for shelter. Do what will make our fear, born of confusion, go away.
vishnu_gita.1.60.sa: वयं शरणमापन्नाः शरणागतवत्सल !। भयं नो मोहजं येन विनश्यति तथा कुरु ॥

vishnu_gita.1.98.m: In honour lies the fear of being brought low; in virtue, the fear of the wicked; in power, the fear of critics; in learning, the fear of rival debaters.
roles: Shows seeing the cost of each gain.
vishnu_gita.1.98.sa: दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु । भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
